title: The Bicycle Repair Shop
description: An old man opens a bicycle repair shop and teaches young people.
instructions: Read the text about a bicycle repair shop, then choose the best answer (A, B, C or D) for each question.

paragraphs.text: Mr Okafor worked in a car factory for forty years. When he stopped working, he felt bored at home. He loved bicycles, so he opened a small repair shop in his garage. The shop is open every afternoon except Sunday.

People bring him bicycles with flat tyres, broken chains and old brakes. Mr Okafor fixes most of them in less than an hour. He does not ask for much money. Sometimes, if a child cannot pay, he repairs the bike for free.

One day, a teenager called Jake brought in a very old bike. It was rusty, and the wheels did not turn. Mr Okafor showed Jake how to clean it and change the parts. After two weeks of work together, the bike looked like new.
Now Jake comes to the shop after school three times a week. He is learning to repair bicycles himself. Mr Okafor says Jake is his best student. Jake wants to open his own shop one day.

Last spring, Jake had an idea. Many old bicycles were in people's garages, and nobody used them. He asked his neighbours to give them to the shop. In two months, people brought more than thirty old bikes. Some were very dirty, and some had no wheels, but Mr Okafor smiled. 'We can fix most of them,' he said. 'But we are going to need more help.'

Every Saturday, Jake and Mr Okafor worked on the bikes together. Some of Jake's friends from school came to help too. They painted the bikes in bright colours, and they put new tyres and lights on them. The garage was full of noise and laughter. Mr Okafor said he felt younger than he did in many years.

In the summer, they gave the bikes to children from poor families in the town. Many of the children never had a bike before, and some of them cried with happiness. A local newspaper wrote a story about them, with a big photo of Mr Okafor and Jake. Now people from other towns call the shop for advice. Mr Okafor is not bored any more. 'I am busier now than when I worked at the factory,' he says with a laugh.
